answer: On an agent task exchange, each new identity locks a 200-credit stake that vests for 30 days. Auditors sample 5% of jobs, like copper price forecasts or voyage routing plans, embed the outputs, and link identities whose answers stay semantically near-identical across tasks, so a paraphrased walnut yield model still clusters. Slashing hits the whole linked cluster: 1,000 fakes risk 200,000 credits, and each added fake raises both stake and detection odds.
